agent_return.guard: In nextFullMoon, after computing fullMs and constructing const result = new Date(fullMs), a check `if (Number.isNaN(result.getTime())) throw new TypeError('nextFullMoon result is outside the representable Date range');` runs before return. Sits next to the existing input guard, same Number.isNaN(...getTime()) idiom, same TypeError class. Meeus math (truePhaseJD, lunationK, toMs) untouched.
tests_added: nextFullMoon throws TypeError (not a silent Invalid Date) when the result exceeds the Date range -- pins that new Date(8640000000000000) throws TypeError and specifically NOT RangeError

nextFullMoon still succeeds for a valid Date just under the top of the range -- pins that the guard does not over-trigger; top-of-range minus 40 days still returns a valid Date whose toISOString() works
agent_uncertainties: did not add a lower-boundary (-8.64e15) test; the guard covers both directions since new Date(ms) is invalid for |ms| > 8.64e15 regardless of sign, but only the top-of-range case was empirically checked
the new error message wording has no prior precedent in the repo to match against; the agent inverted the existing 'nextFullMoon expects a valid Date' phrasing as a judgement call
